sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: GenXAI is an acquisition-led enterprise analytics and implementation group, not a verified pure-play recurring AI software business. At the 19 October close of ₹86, market value is ₹154.32 crore and current-share FY2026 owner P/E is 11.33×. Those modest-looking multiples do not resolve the quality question: FY2026 CFO is −₹6.29 crore, acquisitions obscure underlying growth, and material related-asset mapping remains unexplained. BQS, GQS and IAS are NS, not zero or a neutral estimate. The existing funding diagnostic survives credible stress after the IPO, so there is no modeled G3 failure. The conditional action is research watchlist only, pending a reconciled group/owner cash and asset bridge. [S1][S3][S5][S14]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Cutoff 20 October 2026; last exchange session 19 October. Company identity is GenXAI Analytics Limited, NSE SME GENXAI, ISIN INE1W0N01014, listed 12 June 2026. FY2026 annual accounts are the latest reviewed audited period; no September results or October bank balance is implied. G1 Integrity is Conditional: the disclosure omission and RPT mapping need explanation, without an evidenced misconduct conclusion. G2 Financial reliability is Hold for investment scoring: audited face figures are usable, but entity/claim notes are not sufficiently reconciled for owner value. G3 Funding and survival is Conditional, not Fail: all diagnostic cases remain funded under stated cash-pooling and drawn-CC renewal assumptions. G4 Tradability is Conditional: actual trades are observed but lots, sparse participation and execution uncertainty matter. Confidence is high in the exact checked filings and quote, medium in historical group cash interpretation, and low in organic growth, incremental returns and owner valuation. [S1–S7][S14][S15]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV NS, MOAT 5, REV NS, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 2, BAL 6, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R/D/P NS and L 5. BQS known contribution is 2.68 with 56% coverage and 3.12–7.08 mathematical missing-factor bounds. GQS known contribution is 2.15 with 45% coverage; its uncapped 2.70–7.65 range is capped at 5 because persistent CASH 2 applies. IAS has 10% coverage, a known 0.50 liquidity contribution and 1.40–9.50 generic missing-factor bounds. These bounds are not ratings, probabilities or targets. No weights are redistributed; Q would equal final BQS, not an invented substitute. All final composites remain NS. No historical factor receives 9–10 from this short, changing perimeter. Exact formulas and factor-specific counterevidence accompany the record. [S1][S2][S14]

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: The core is enterprise performance management, analytics, ERP/planning implementation, IT consulting, staffing, support and related digital delivery. Partner-led skills can generate follow-on implementation/support work, while the group is investing in sales-incentive, invoice-management and AI platforms. Product names and partner logos do not establish SaaS economics: verified ARR, churn, paid-seat retention, product gross margin and subscription share were not available. FY2026 export revenue is ₹44.01 crore, 49.83% of sales. The group owns 100% of several subsidiaries, 70% of Softgrid, 51% of Logimetrix, Veear Projects, Veear Analytics Inc and Vaikom, and 90% of Rigved. These interests cannot be valued as if every rupee of group profit belongs to listed shareholders. [S1][S2][S8]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: Enterprise planning integrations, knowledge of customer processes and certified delivery skills can raise switching inconvenience. The evidence nevertheless supports a useful but contestable service franchise, not a structural AI monopoly. The prospectus says customers do not sign long-term/exclusive arrangements. For the nine months to December 2025, the top customer supplied 20.67% of revenue, top five 61.07% and top ten 74.36%. The annual presentation’s broad client and sector claims do not negate this concentration. AION-Tech and Latent View are issuer-selected contextual peers; their size, mix and economics differ, so their multiples are not automatic valuation anchors. A stronger moat finding requires paid renewals, identifiable proprietary-product revenue and evidence of pricing/retention through competition. [S2][S8]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: Restated revenue is ₹16.5701/24.0695/28.5318/88.3244 crore for FY2023–FY2026. Reported three-year CAGR is 74.68% and the latest annual increase is ₹59.79 crore, 209.56%. This is not the selected organic scoring basis: new majority-owned businesses entered the group in FY2026. Parent-only revenue rose 27.90% to ₹33.04 crore, but named sales to GenXAI Inc and Veear Analytics Inc total ₹9.1535 crore; mechanically subtracting those produces ₹23.8854 crore, below the prior parent total. That subtraction is a diagnostic, not an organic decline conclusion, because delivery routing and eliminations changed. A business-by-business acquisition-date and same-client bridge is missing, therefore REV is NS. FY2023–FY2024 restated 45.26% growth is a positive older comparison; it cannot establish the current group trajectory. No unsupported five/ten-year CAGR is used. [S1][S2]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: The IPO supports actual funding capacity: ₹7.20 crore working capital, ₹3 crore debt repayment, ₹28.37 crore development and ₹7.64 crore general corporate purposes. The monitor records ₹3 crore debt repayment and ₹1.35 crore transferred for WC, of which ₹0.95 crore salaries were paid by June and remaining related expenses in July. Development funding is for AI Cloud Engine and sales-incentive products, including people and hardware/software costs, not simply factory capacity. The accessible runway includes cross-selling and enterprise transformation, but a ₹28.37 crore budget is not customer demand or proof of high returns. Existing development assets are ₹9.766 crore; cohort revenue, maintenance burden and incremental invested-capital reconciliation remain unavailable. CAP is NS rather than a high score inferred from headline ROCE. [S1][S5]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: On 17 June, the issuer and merchant bankers acknowledged that the prospectus omitted a relationship between director Raj Kishor Khaware and sellers of Veear Projects and Tech. They described the omission as inadvertent and the transaction as arm’s-length, with unchanged commercial terms and no effect on IPO objects or shareholder rights. This is an established disclosure correction, not proof of abuse. The 19 June filing corrected numerous financial-note presentations, including EPS, ageing basis, benefit obligations and related-party disclosures. On 1 October, the specific AGM outcome says the GenXAI Inc material RPT authorization was not approved; the detailed vote has 217,390 for and 553,200 against. This does not establish illegality of existing contracts. The 18 lakh ESOP authorization passed; the exercise formula is the lower of ₹60 or 70% of grant-date market price, subject to face value, with one-to-five-year vesting. No actual grant or future exercise cash is assumed in the base case. A 29 September filing reports the managing director buying 14,400 shares; insider buying is not evidence that the accounting questions are resolved. [S1][S3][S4][S6][S7][S13]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY2026 operating EBITDA, excluding other income, is ₹23.9423 crore at 27.11%; operating EBIT is ₹22.6293 crore. Group PAT ₹17.2666 crore includes ₹3.6478 crore NCI, leaving ₹13.6188 crore for owners. EPS on current issued shares is ₹7.59, not the reported weighted-average ₹10.58. Three-year FY2024–FY2026 CFO totals −₹1.5144 crore against ₹26.4688 crore group PAT; cash capex is ₹18.7735 crore, producing a −₹20.2879 crore CFO-less-capex proxy. FY2025 original prospectus CFO ₹4.0831 crore/CFI −₹6.1727 crore becomes ₹4.3779/−₹6.4675 crore in the annual comparative, a two-sided ₹0.2948 crore loans/advances reclassification, not lost cash. June’s intermediate rent and liability presentation corrections are retained separately. FY2026 receivables imply 106.58 sales days; 22.01% are aged six-to-twelve months and ₹0.7946 crore are disputed but considered good. The June clarification bases ageing on invoice dates where contractual due dates were not maintained; these buckets do not automatically mean overdue debt. Unbilled assets ₹3.8151 crore, employee/other advances ₹7.9079 crore and accrued related-party interest ₹1.8524 crore need collection evidence. Software capitalization and unbilled revenue are audit KAMs, not qualifications. The group audit is unmodified and relies on other auditors for eight subsidiaries. The annual RPT note labels ₹896.07 lakh as a long-term related-party loan, versus ₹123.74 lakh in the face long-loans/advances category. That mapping is unresolved; no cash-diversion allegation follows. The ₹9 lakh FY2025 cash face/note difference is separately bounded and not the sole reason for the scoring hold. [S1][S2][S4][S10]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: The observed ₹86 quote implies ₹154.3150 crore market capitalization and 11.33× FY2026 owner earnings; dividing by total group PAT would incorrectly yield 8.94×. March leverage ratios are historical, not October net cash: gross debt ₹16.2499 crore, cash/bank ₹4.1213 crore, and a further ₹2.7067 crore long deposits. The model conservatively withholds all ₹4.5471 crore term/long deposits and retains IPO development restrictions. The June monitor places ₹30 crore in a fixed deposit maturing 16 July 2027. Baseline authorized-use access before maturity is conditional, and a no-early-redemption case is tested separately. Its common bridge gives modeled 19 October unrestricted cash ₹18.2682 crore and earmarked cash ₹25.1361 crore, neither an observed balance. Bear/base/bull revenue paths are −5/3/5/5/5%, 18/17/15/13/12%, and 28/25/22/20/18%; EBITDA margins 18/25/29%. Monthly flows include taxes, all opening WC claims, legacy gratuity, principal, interest, collateral, maintenance, development and dilution sensitivity. All three fund under assumptions, but entity allocation, preference rights and related-asset reconciliation prevent a defensible owner fair value or shareholder IRR. Conditional P/E grids explicitly assume 60/78.87/90% owner profit shares and 8/12/18× exits; they are not price targets and do not add group cash on top of earnings value. At 12× and unchanged shares, a 15% five-year hurdle needs owner PAT ₹25.8652 crore, 13.69% annual growth from FY2026. At 8× it needs ₹38.7978 crore, 23.29% growth; at 18× ₹17.2435 crore, 4.83%. This is an earnings hurdle, not a financing proof. [S1][S5][S14][S15]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: The credible operating risk is a concentrated client loss or delay combined with an immature product spend. A restrained survival case stops optional new development/growth capex, applies a 15% initial revenue decline, 17% EBITDA, 25 extra collection days phased over six months and an inventory floor. It retains earmarked money for its authorized purpose rather than freeing it for payroll. Minimum post-entry free cash is ₹18.0313 crore; excluding foreign operating cash gives ₹17.1173 crore. Even a separate gross recall of the remaining ₹9.5702 crore current debt leaves a modeled ₹8.6394 crore minimum. A separate no-early-FD-redemption case also freezes project spending until the disclosed July 2027 maturity, reserves the additional ₹1.63 crore nonproject FD component, and excludes foreign operating cash; its minimum is ₹15.4873 crore. These results do not establish that subsidiaries can legally transfer cash or lenders renew facilities, but they do not justify a G3 Fail. Separate boundaries replace ₹7.9079 crore of unrecovered advances and pay a ₹2.736 crore combined tax/ROC/gross-guarantee amount. The guarantee boundary may overlap consolidated debt and is not added to baseline debt. Permanent equity loss can still arise from product impairment, weak owner earnings, acquisition underperformance, dilution and a lower exit multiple. No precise owner downside or liquidation recovery is claimed while the asset and preference bridge is unresolved. [S1][S2][S5]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: Five- and ten-fold price outcomes over five years require 37.97% and 58.49% annual share-price returns. At unchanged 17,943,610 shares and 12× exit P/E, owner PAT must reach ₹64.2979 crore for 5× or ₹128.5959 crore for 10×, equivalent to 36.40%/56.68% annual profit growth from FY2026. At an assumed 15% owner net margin this implies group revenue ₹428.65/857.31 crore, but that margin and minority allocation are not established. An 18× exit lowers required owner PAT to ₹42.8653/85.7306 crore while requiring a sustained premium; 8× raises it to ₹96.4469/192.8938 crore. Full 18 lakh option exercise increases shares by 10.03% and raises required earnings proportionately; the ₹10.8 crore exercise-cash sensitivity assumes ₹60, not a current right to receive money. Product commercialization, funding, sustained organic demand and owner economics would all need proof. No multibagger label or probability is justified. [S1][S14][S15]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Review the first September half-year filing and IPO monitor when published, not as an already scheduled automation. Priority checks are: (1) bank-by-bank unrestricted versus earmarked cash, exact issue costs and development milestones; (2) reconciliation of related loans, interest, employee/other advances and the annual cash-note difference; (3) revenue/EBIT/PAT/CFO by acquired entity, acquisition date, ownership and intercompany elimination; (4) conversion of aged/disputed receivables and unbilled balances into cash; (5) published explanation and operational effect of the rejected GenXAI Inc RPT authorization; (6) ESOP grants, actual exercise terms and subsidiary preference rights. Thesis-positive evidence is sustained owner cash conversion without new external rescue and paid product adoption. Thesis-negative evidence is unexplained fresh advances, further collection ageing, development spending without saleable output, or source corrections that alter cash/claims materially. Recheck lot, surveillance and live depth before any investment decision. [S1][S5][S6][S14][S15]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Classification: acquisition-led services and product-development transition with unresolved owner economics. Status: completed conditional research, not a scoreable investment recommendation and not eligible for numeric composite ranking. It is neither an evidenced compounder nor an evidenced fraud/default case. The fresh IPO improves modeled funding resilience, but a lower headline P/E cannot compensate for an unverified organic growth and capital-allocation bridge. Conditional action: retain on a research watchlist, require the specific reconciliations and first post-IPO cash evidence, then rerun all gates/factors and owner valuation. The illustrative ₹5 lakh liquidity reference is not a proposed allocation, and no trade or company outreach is implied.

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary anchors are the final prospectus, signed FY2026 results/annual report, June corrections, IPO monitoring report and October AGM disclosures. Older original and restated accounts are kept separate; the FY2025 scanned annual file was obtained but not used as an independently transcribed numerical source. The issuer older-report index returned 403 on a later retrieval; no restriction was bypassed, and a comparable five/ten-year current-group record is not claimed. Financial-model assumptions are explicit rather than represented as issuer forecasts: cash pooling, drawn-CC continuation, monthly operating timing, 27% tax, 2.5% revenue maintenance, staged product amortization from October 2028, retention of uncertain assets and assumed preference settlement. Claim maps preserve government/tax credits, statutory/employee/expense liabilities, interest, deposits, minority preferences, contingencies and proposed investments once each. Open questions remain material to value, so no return/valuation certainty is manufactured. Exact source locators and reproducible arithmetic accompany this dossier. [S1–S16]

limitations: June monitor places30 crore in a July 2027-maturity FD. Baseline assumes it can fund authorized project spending before maturity. An explicit no-early-redemption case freezes development and additionally reserves1.63 crore of nonproject FD until maturity; no access guarantee is inferred.
The model is a complete as-reported group cash diagnostic, not verified accessible parent liquidity or a fair value.
All post-March operating, cash and debt balances except disclosed IPO transactions are assumptions; no September results were available at cutoff.

Product amortization begins October 2028 over five years of accumulated development cost; commencement/useful life are analytical assumptions. Maintenance equals2.5% of revenue; growth/product spending is separate.
Group cash pooling and existing drawn CC renewal are conditional. No additional sanctioned headroom is assumed.
Restricted March term deposits, government credits, other loans, related interest and security assets are retained without presumed recovery or terminal bonus.
Product-development proceeds and accrued interest remain earmarked. Canceling development does not release funds to core operations.
All IPO cash fees beyond prepaid 135.39 lakh are conservatively settled at IPO; this pays the later outstanding fee budget early. No double cash charge of prepaid fees.
Opening employee/other advances are not automatically released on declining revenue; no assertion they are all operating assets is made.

Disclosed MSME interest 0.61 lakh is conservatively paid separately; possible inclusion in another accrued expense is unresolved, so this is a small additional model reserve, not a revised issuer liability.
Current taxes are settled separately from government credits; no unsupported offset.
Opening gratuity is settled over a modeled schedule; future benefit cost is included in EBITDA and paid, not used to erase opening deficit.
Redeemable preference 81 lakh is paid in March 2031 only as an explicit assumption. Contractual redemption, CCPS conversion and subsidiary cash mobility remain missing.
Existing debt maturity beyond first-year current portion is approximated; early-recall boundary is separate, not a forecast.
Owner P/E grid retains debt via post-interest profits; no extra addition of group cash or subtraction of debt. No IRR or IAS is assigned because entity allocation is unresolved.
Related-party loan disclosure 896.07 lakh exceeds face noncurrent loan category 123.74 lakh. Model maps audited face totals once; the discrepancy prevents claims-complete owner valuation.
